cli.services_heavy.heavy.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.heavy.note: Summary of `lop services heavy`. The heavy-job slot is a machine-wide lease that heavy builds/tests queue for; keep 'slot' as one countable noun used consistently across this namespace.

cli.services_heavy.heavy_description.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.heavy_description.note: Group-page description. 'wait', 'run' and 'status' are literal subcommand names and stay untranslated. 'wait' never takes a slot; 'run' frees it when the command exits.

cli.services_heavy.wait.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.wait.note: wait only observes: it must be clear the slot is NOT taken.

cli.services_heavy.run.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.run.note: run holds the slot for exactly the command's lifetime.

cli.services_heavy.status.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.status.note: pid stays literal. 'age' means how long the holder has held the slot.

cli.services_heavy.timeout.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.timeout.note: {wait_seconds} is a number formatted by code (e.g. 900); the trailing 's' is the seconds unit. {env_name} is an environment variable name, literal.

cli.services_heavy.command.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions

cli.services_heavy.holder.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.holder.note: One indented row per holder under the status line. {slot} is a slot index number, {holder} names the holder (e.g. 'pid 123' or 'session/123'), {age} is a compact duration such as 8s or 3m05s, {command} is the command line, literal. Keep the two leading spaces.

cli.services_heavy.no_command.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.no_command.note: Printed when `run` is given no command; nothing was queued. `--` and the example command are literal.

cli.services_heavy.events_header.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.events_header.note: Heading above the last few heavy-job lease audit events in `lop services heavy status`. {path} is a file path, literal. Keep the two leading spaces and the trailing colon.

cli.services_heavy.event_line.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.event_line.note: One audit event under the heading. {time} is an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, {record} is a literal log excerpt (event name and key=value fields such as take slot=0 pid=123); both stay untranslated. Keep the four leading spaces; usually nothing to translate.

cli.services_heavy.no_events.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.no_events.note: Shown instead of the event list when the heavy-job lease audit log has no events yet. {path} is a file path, literal. 'lease events' = slot taken/released/timed out/reclaimed records. Keep the two leading spaces.

cli.services_heavy.audit_row.tone: terse, operator-facing, preserves safety and command distinctions
cli.services_heavy.audit_row.note: One-line readiness row in `lop services status`. 'heavy jobs audit' labels the heavy-job lease audit trail. {record} is a literal log excerpt (event name plus key=value fields, untranslated), {age} a compact duration such as 8s or 3m05s, {path} a file path.
